walkthrough: Goal: enlarge a small drawing three times and deliver it at 4x, its lines as crisp as if drawn that large; move part of it again later without it going soft.

Entry and gestures are S20's: on a canvas with a short ink line, tap Transform (the arrow after Selection); the frame, its corner handles and the turn handle appear; drag the bottom-right corner out until the frame is about three times as large.

What appears: while the pen drags, the line grows with the frame; when the pen lifts the line shows with the same clean edge it had before, now three times as thick (nothing is resampled: the line is drawn again where it moved).
Done: tap Transform again: one step of the drawing. Actions > Share, 4×, Save PNG…: the file's line edges are one file pixel wide, not blurred over twelve.

Again: Selection, Rectangle around the left half, Transform, drag inside the frame to move it down: only that half moves, the right half stays; Brush commits it and nothing is selected. Then Transform without a selection, Rotate 45° and Transform again: the half moved earlier turns with the rest (transforms nest).
Undo: one undo takes the last transform back, another the selection's; redo brings each again. Reopen after the system closed the app: everything is where it was left, the line still crisp at 4x.
Failure and cancel are S20's: hidden, locked or empty layers refuse with a notice; Reset or undo inside the tool puts the content back before committing.
